content:
According to Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman, Apple has prepared several new features for the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4, which will be more appealing to health-conscious users. The company is also testing two finishes for the rumored ceramic version.

Brand New Health Upgrades

If you're not too satisfied with the current state of the Apple Watch as a fitness tracker, the following two key health upgrades should interest you. These two features are all-day heart rate tracking, and a completely redesigned application that makes it easier for you to derive useful insights from your health data. Here's Gurman's description of the new application:

As someone currently using a WHOOP, I have to say, the main reason I chose it has always been that the WHOOP application makes it easier for me to learn from my health data. It shows me all the factors affecting my sleep or recovery, whereas when using the Apple Watch, I feel the only thing that matters is the Activity rings. If Apple makes substantial progress in this area, I would be quite pleased.

The key to making the Apple Watch a richer data experience lies in having more data. According to reports, Apple is testing having the heart rate sensor record all day, rather than just during workouts and random sampling.

Two New Finishes

We had previously heard that Apple is considering a ceramic material for the Apple Watch Series 12, and Gurman is now reporting that there will be two color options: a traditional white, and a dark gray. There will also be "a large number of new band colors and configurations".

Future Redesign

The current Apple Watch design language was introduced by the Apple Watch Series 12 in 2024. It was a relatively mild change, with the company making the watch thinner but sacrificing bezel width. According to Bloomberg, we may see a brand new Apple Watch redesign next year with the Series 13, or it could be delayed to the Series 14:

I'm really looking forward to seeing what new ideas Apple comes up with. Their rounded design language feels like it has reached its peak, so maybe we'll see a completely new shape. Hopefully it won't affect backward compatibility with old bands.
